status: Suggestions for an officer to approve, never decisions.
about: Routes out of temporary accommodation and suitability checks from official guidance and legislation only, for synthetic household records. Each pathway and check has a stable id, a condition a program can evaluate (field, operator, value) and the same condition in words. Paragraph numbers are as read on 21 October 2026 and can move when GOV.UK updates the code. Official links, with the date each was read, are in references.json.

condition_language.gte: field is a number at or above value
condition_language.lt: field is a number below value
condition_language.lte: field is a number at or below value

condition_language.nonempty: field is a list or text with something in it

general_checks.text: Confirm which duty the household is owed: interim accommodation under s.188(1), the relief duty under s.189B or the main housing duty under s.193(2). The pathways that end a duty assume the main housing duty.
Take account of the wishes, needs and circumstances of the household, as the code asks when assessing affordability (Code 17.48), and record them before any step.

pathways.title: Social housing through the allocation scheme (Part 6)
pathways.summary: An offer of social housing under the council's allocation scheme. Accepting a suitable Part 6 offer ends the main housing duty.
pathways.applies_when_text: Every household in TA; the officer confirms the duty owed.

reasons.text: The allocation scheme must give reasonable preference to people who are homeless within the meaning of Part 7 and to people owed the main housing duty under s.193(2) (s.166A(3)(a) and (b)).
The main housing duty ends when the applicant accepts a suitable offer of accommodation under Part 6 (s.193(6)(c); Code 15.38(a)).

officer_checks.text: Check that the household is eligible for an allocation and qualifies under the allocation scheme (allocation guidance, paragraphs 3.2 and 3.30).
Check that any offer is suitable for the household, including space, location and affordability (s.193(7F); Code chapter 17).

If an offer is to be a final offer, check that it is made in writing and says that it is a final offer, and that the household has been told the possible consequences of refusal or acceptance and of the right to ask for a review of suitability (s.193(7) and (7A); Code 15.38(c)).
Check whether the household has obligations on its current accommodation that it cannot end before it would have to take up the offer (s.193(7F) and (8)).

notes.when_text: The record lists physical ill health and disability, mental health problems or a learning disability.
notes.text: The scheme must also give reasonable preference to people who need to move on medical or welfare grounds, including grounds relating to a disability (s.166A(3)(d)); check what the household's medical or welfare needs require of an offer, including any adaptations (Code 17.5).

any.value: homeless as a result of domestic abuse
at risk of or has experienced domestic abuse

notes.when_text: The priority need is homelessness as a result of domestic abuse, or the record lists domestic abuse.
notes.text: The allocation guidance gives, as an example of urgent need, people who are homeless and need urgent rehousing as a result of violence or threats of violence (allocation guidance, paragraph 4.13); check whether the scheme gives additional preference.

pathways.title: Private rented sector offer
pathways.summary: An offer of a private tenancy, arranged by the council to bring the main housing duty to an end. The duty ends whether the household accepts or refuses it, if the conditions are met.
pathways.applies_when_text: Every household in TA; the officer confirms the duty owed.

reasons.text: The main housing duty ends if the applicant accepts or refuses a private rented sector offer that meets the conditions in s.193(7AA) to (7AC) (Code 15.38(b)).

From 1 May 2026, for a tenancy that is not social housing, the offer is of an assured tenancy from a private landlord with no minimum fixed term, and the reapplication duty in s.195A no longer applies (Renters' Rights Act 2025, s.25, commenced for those tenancies by SI 2026/421).

For a social housing tenancy from a private registered provider, the law remains as it was until the reforms start for those tenancies, expected in October 2027 (Code overview, paras 6 and 7): an assured shorthold tenancy of at least 12 months, and the s.195A duty if the household reapplies within 2 years.

officer_checks.text: Check which rules apply before the offer is made: for a tenancy that is not social housing, from 1 May 2026, an assured tenancy with no minimum fixed term and no s.195A duty; for a social housing tenancy from a private registered provider, the earlier rules until the reforms start for it (Code overview, paras 6 and 7); and the s.195A duty still applies where the household accepted a private rented sector offer before 1 May 2026 (SI 2026/421, regulation 10).

Check each condition in article 3 of the 2012 Order before approving the offer: reasonable physical condition; electrical equipment that meets Schedule 1 to the Electrical Equipment (Safety) Regulations 2016; reasonable fire safety and carbon monoxide precautions; a landlord who is a fit and proper person; any licence a house in multiple occupation, or additional licensing, needs; a valid energy performance certificate; a current gas safety record; and an adequate written tenancy agreement given to the council (Code 17.16 to 17.17).

Check the location against article 2 of the 2012 Order: the distance from the district, disruption to work, caring responsibilities or education, access to the medical facilities and support the household uses, and access to local services, amenities and transport.
Check that the rent is affordable for the household, taking account of its income and essential living costs (Code 17.47 and 17.48).

Check that the household is told in writing of the possible consequences of refusal or acceptance and of the right to ask for a review of suitability (s.193(7AB); Code 15.38(b)), and, where the s.195A duty applies to the offer, of the duties owed if it reapplies within 2 years.

Check that the council is satisfied the accommodation is suitable, and that the household has no obligations on its current accommodation it cannot end in time, before it approves the offer (s.193(7F) and (8)).

notes.text: Check the disruption a move would cause to the children's education (2012 Order, article 2(b)).

notes.when_text: The record lists one or more support needs.
notes.text: Check that the support and medical services the household relies on stay within reach (2012 Order, article 2(c)).

pathways.title: Supported housing
pathways.summary: Accommodation provided alongside support, supervision or care, for a household whose support needs it would meet.
pathways.applies_when_text: The record lists one or more support needs.

reasons.text: Supported housing is provided alongside support, supervision or care, and the groups it serves include people with mental ill health, people fleeing domestic abuse, people recovering from drug or alcohol dependence and young people with a support need (national statement of expectations).
The national statement of expectations is not statutory: it sets out what the government expects and suggests good practice.

officer_checks.text: Check that the household's support and housing needs have been assessed before any referral (national statement of expectations), and ask whether it wants supported housing.

Check how a move would affect the main housing duty: it ends if the household accepts a suitable Part 6 offer (s.193(6)(c)) or voluntarily ceases to occupy the accommodation provided as its only or principal home (s.193(6)(d)); explain this to the household before any move.
Check that any accommodation used to meet a duty is suitable for the household (Code chapter 17).

notes.when_text: The household has children or includes a pregnant woman.
notes.text: The code says supported accommodation with shared facilities will not normally be suitable for longer-term placements of families with pregnant women or children (Code 2.52); check whether self-contained supported housing could be found.

when.value: at risk of or has experienced domestic abuse

notes.text: Check safety and location risks with the household before any referral, using the code's chapter on domestic abuse (Code chapter 21).

notes.when_text: The record lists a young person needing support, or a young applicant or care leaver.
notes.text: Use the code's chapter on young people, including those with care experience (Code chapter 22).

suitability_checks.when_text: In B&B, with children or a pregnant woman in the household.
suitability_checks.text: B&B counts as suitable for an applicant with family commitments only where no other accommodation is available, and then for no more than 6 weeks in total, and the code says to use it only as a last resort (2003 Order, articles 3 and 4; Code 17.35 and 17.38). The record does not show how long the household has been in B&B: check the time used against the 6 weeks limit, and secure other suitable accommodation before it is reached.

suitability_checks.when_text: In B&B, with an applicant aged 16 or 17.
suitability_checks.text: The code rules out B&B for 16 and 17 year old applicants, even on an emergency basis (Code 17.42). The record holds the priority need at acceptance, not the applicant's age now: check the age, and check that other suitable accommodation is secured.

suitability_checks.when_text: In B&B, with a care leaver as the applicant.
suitability_checks.text: The code says B&B, hotels and nightly-let accommodation with shared facilities are not suitable for care leavers aged under 25, and should be used only in exceptional circumstances and for short periods, with close management and oversight throughout where their use cannot be avoided (Code 22.48): check that other suitable accommodation is secured.

suitability_checks.when_text: The applicant was aged 16 or 17 at acceptance.
suitability_checks.text: If the applicant is still 16 or 17, check that children's services are involved: section 20 of the Children Act 1989 places a duty on children's services authorities to accommodate a child in need, and in almost all circumstances a homeless 16 or 17 year old would be a child in need; the joint statutory guidance on 16 and 17 year olds sets out the duties (Code 22.6 and 22.7).

suitability_checks.when_text: Placed outside the council's own district.
suitability_checks.text: So far as reasonably practicable, the council secures accommodation in its own district (s.208(1)). For a placement outside it, check that written notice went to the council where the accommodation is within 14 days of the accommodation being made available (s.208(2) to (4)), and check the location against article 2 of the 2012 Order and Code chapter 17.

Check space and arrangement against the household's size, including the room and space standards in Part 10 of the Housing Act 1985, and check that the accommodation is free of Category 1 hazards and affordable (Code 17.4, 17.27 to 17.29, 17.47 and 17.48).

suitability_checks.when_text: The record lists physical ill health and disability.
suitability_checks.text: Consider carefully the suitability of accommodation for a household with medical or physical needs (Code 17.5).
